text:
A parallel plate capacitor with plate area 'A' and distance of separation 'd' is filled with a dielectric. What is the capacity of the capacitor when permittivity of the dielectric varies as :

$ε(x)=ε_{0}+kx$, for $\left (0<x\leq \frac{d}{2}\right )$

$ε(x)=ε_{0}+k(d-x)$, for $\left (\frac{d}{2}\leq x\leq d\right )$
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 25th July Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
[IMG]
 

Taking an element of width dx at a distance x(x < d/2) from left plate

$dc=\frac{(ε_{0}+kx)A}{dx}$

Capacitance of half of the capacitor

$\frac{1}{C}=\int\limits _{0}^{d/2}\frac{1}{dc}=\frac{1}{A}\int\limits _{0}^{d/2}\frac{dx}{ε_{0}+kx}$

$\frac{1}{C}=\frac{1}{kA}\ln \left (\frac{ε_{0}+kd/2}{ε_{0}}\right )$

Capacitance of second half will be same

$C_{eq}=\frac{C}{2}=\frac{kA}{2\ln \left (\frac{2ε0+kd}{2ε0}\right )}$

text: Two wires of same length and radius are joined end to end and loaded. The Young's moduli of the materials of the two wires are $Y_{1}$ and $Y_{2}$. The combination behaves as a single wire then its Young's modulus is :

In series combination $\Delta$l = $\Deltal_{1} +$ $\Deltal_{2}$

$Y=\frac{F/A}{\Delta l/l}\Rightarrow \Delta l=\frac{Fl}{AY}$

$\Rightarrow \Delta l\propto \frac{l}{Y}$

Equivalent length of rod after joining is = 2l

$\Delta l=\Delta l_{1}+\Delta l_{2}$

$\frac{l_{eq}}{Y_{eq}}=\frac{l}{Y_{1}}+\frac{l}{Y_{2}}\Rightarrow \frac{2l}{Y}=\frac{l}{Y_{1}}+\frac{l}{Y_{2}}$

$\therefore$ $Y=\frac{2Y_{1}Y_{2}}{Y_{1}+Y_{2}}$

text:
In the Young's double slit experiment, the distance between the slits varies in time as 
$d(t) = d_{0} + a_{0} \sin ω$t; where $d_{0}$, $ω$ and $a_{0}$ are constants. The difference between the largest fringe width and the smallest fringe width obtained over time is given as :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 25th July Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Fringe Width, $β=\frac{λD}{d}$

$β_{\max }\Rightarrow d_{\min }$ and $β_{\min }\Rightarrow d_{\max }$

$d=d_{0}+a_{0}\sin ωt$

$d_{\max }=d_{0}+a_{0}$ and $d_{\min }=d_{0}-a_{0}$

$\therefore$ $β_{\min }=\frac{λD}{d_{0}+a_{0}}$ and

$β_{\max }-β_{\min }=\frac{λD}{d_{0}-a_{0}}-\frac{λD}{d_{0}+a_{0}}=\frac{2λDa_{0}}{d_{0}^{2}-a_{0}^{2}}$

text: Water droplets are coming from an open tap at a particular rate. The spacing between a droplet observed at $4^{th}$ second after its fall to the next droplet is 34.3 m. At what rate the droplets are coming from the tap ? (Take $g = 9.8 m/s^{2})$

In $4 \sec . 1^{st}$ drop will travel

$\Rightarrow \frac{1}{2}$ $\times$ (9.8) $\times$ $(4)^{2} = 78.4 m$

$\therefore$ $2^{nd}$ drop would have travelled

$\Rightarrow$ 78.4 $-$ 34.3 = 44.1 m.

Time for $2^{nd}$ drop

$\Rightarrow \frac{1}{2}(9.8)t^{2} = 44.1$

t = 3 sec

$\therefore$ each drop has a time gap of 1 sec

$\therefore$ 1 drop per sec

text:
Student A and student B used two screw gauges of equal pitch and 100 equal circular divisions to measure the radius of a given wire. The actual value of the radius of the wire is 0.322 cm. The absolute value of the difference between the final circular scale readings observed by the students A and B is $______________$.

[Figure shows position of reference 'O' when jaws of screw gauge are closed]

Given pitch = 0.1 cm.


[IMG]
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 25th July Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The least count of each gauge is

$\text{LC}=\dfrac{\text{pitch}}{N}=\dfrac{0.1\text{cm}}{100}=0.001\text{cm}$

With the jaws closed, gauge A reads 5 circular divisions against the reference O, so its zero error is positive: $e_{A}=+5\times 0.001=+0.005\text{cm}$.

Gauge B reads 92 divisions, which is 8 divisions short of the circular-scale zero, so its zero error is negative: $e_{B}=-(100-92)\times 0.001=-0.008\text{cm}$.

The observed reading equals the true value plus the zero error. Each main-scale division is one pitch, $0.1\text{cm}$.

Gauge A: $0.322+0.005=0.327\text{cm}=0.3\text{cm}+27\times 0.001\text{cm}$, so the circular scale reading is 27.

Gauge B: $0.322-0.008=0.314\text{cm}=0.3\text{cm}+14\times 0.001\text{cm}$, so the circular scale reading is 14.

The absolute difference of the circular scale readings is $|27-14|=13$.

Hence, the answer is 13.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2021 (Online) 25th July Morning Shift

text:
A circular conducting coil of radius 1 m is being heated by the change of magnetic field $\vec{B}$ passing perpendicular to the plane in which the coil is laid. The resistance of the coil is 2 $μ\Omega$. The magnetic field is slowly switched off such that its magnitude changes in time as 

$B=\frac{4}{π}\times 10^{-3}T\left (1-\frac{t}{100}\right )$

The energy dissipated by the coil before the magnetic field is switched off completely is $E = ___________ mJ$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 25th July Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$𝜙=\vec{B}.\vec{S}$

$𝜙=\frac{4}{π}\times 10^{-3}\left (1-\frac{t}{100}\right ).πR^{2}$

$𝜙=4\times 10^{-3}\times (1)^{2}\left (1-\frac{t}{100}\right )$

$ε=\frac{-d𝜙}{dt}$

$ε=\frac{-d}{dt}\left (4\times 10^{-3}\left (1-\frac{t}{100}\right )\right )$

$ε=4\times 10^{-3}\left (\frac{1}{100}\right )=4\times 10^{-5}V$

When B = 0

$1-\frac{t}{100}=0$

t = 100 sec

Heat $=\frac{ε^{2}}{R}t$

Heat $=\frac{(4\times 10^{-5})^{2}}{2\times 10^{-6}}\times 100$ J

Heat $=\frac{16\times 10^{-10}\times 100}{2\times 10^{-6}}$ J

Heat = 0.08 J

Heat = 80 mJ
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2021 (Online) 25th July Morning Shift

text: A particle of mass 1 mg and charge q is lying at the mid-point of two stationary particles kept at a distance '2 m' when each is carrying same charge 'q'. If the free charged particle is displaced from its equilibrium position through distance 'x' (x << 1 m), the particle executes SHM. Its angular frequency of oscillation will be $____________$ $\times$ $10^{5}$ rad/s if $q^{2} = 10 C^{2}$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 25th July Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
[IMG]
 

Net force on free charged particle

$F=\frac{kq^{2}}{(d+x)^{2}}-\frac{kq^{2}}{(d-x)^{2}}$

$F=-kq^{2}\left [\frac{4dx}{(d^{2}-x^{2})^{2}}\right ]$

$a=-\frac{4kq^{2}d}{m}\left (\frac{x}{d^{4}}\right )$

$a=-\left (\frac{4kq^{2}}{md^{3}}\right )x$

So, angular frequency 

$ω=\sqrt{\frac{4kq^{2}}{md^{3}}}$

$ω=\sqrt{\frac{4\times 9\times 10^{9}\times 10}{1\times 10^{-6}\times 1^{3}}}$

$ω=6\times 10^{8}$ rad/sec

$ω=6000\times 10^{5}$ rad/sec
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2021 (Online) 25th July Morning Shift

text:
A particle of mass 'm' is moving in time 't' on a trajectory given by

$\vec{r}=10αt^{2}\hat{i}+5β(t-5)\hat{j}$

Where $α$ and $β$ are dimensional constants.

The angular momentum of the particle becomes the same as it was for t = 0 at time $t = ____________$ seconds.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 25th July Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\vec{r}=10αt^{2}\hat{i}+5β(t-5)\hat{j}$

$\vec{v}=20αt\hat{i}+5β\hat{j}$

$\vec{L}=m(\vec{r}\times \vec{v})$

$=m[10αt^{2}\hat{i}+5β(t-5)\hat{j}]\times [20αt\hat{i}+5β\hat{j}]$

$\vec{L}=m[50αβt^{2}\widehat{k}-100αβ(t^{2}-5t)\widehat{k}]$

At t = 0, $\vec{L}=\vec{0}$

$50αβt^{2}-100αβ(t^{2}-5t)=0$

t $-$ 2 (t $-$ 5) = 0

t = 10 sec
